names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 18 ianuarie, «Sfântul Ierarh Chiril, Arhiepiscopul Alexandriei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Ιανουαρίου, «Άγιοι Αθανάσιος ο Μέγας και Κύριλλος Πατριάρχες Αλεξανδρείας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. јун ст. ст., „Свети Кирил, архиепископ александријски“ — Свети is not a rank and „архиепископ александријски“ is the rank with its see, which `office` and the display name already carry; both come off and the bare forename is left. **THE FOLD IS THE WIDEST THIS WAVE HAS WRITTEN**: `foldchk.py` returns four `sr` holders already — `cyril-of-catania`, `cyril-of-heliopolis`, `cyril-of-jerusalem`, `cyril-the-philosopher` — so this is the fifth on the string. Deliberate: the heading offers nothing fuller, and a form may not be built out of a body.

The name as name page 1221 gives it, «Святитель Кирилл Александрийский», with the grade taken off. Measured with the gate's own fold before it was written: 'александриискии кирилл' has no other holder; the folder's existing Serbian form is the bare «Кирил» and this one is two words.

birth.note: doxologia.ro's life: «Chiril, marele învățător al Bisericii, s-a născut în 378, la Mahalla, în Egipt». The Охридски пролог for 9. јун ст. ст. gives no year of birth and nothing was changed here (5 October 2026).

death.note: The life's note 71 quotes Theophanes the Confessor: «În acest an (446), au murit întru cucernicie Chiril al Alexandriei și Proclu al Constantinopolului.» The same page says the day of his repose is 9 June, on the authority of Christopher of Mitylene's distich, and that 18 January is not the day of his repose. The Охридски пролог for 9. јун ст. ст. — the very day that argument names — states a different year flat: „Представио се Господу 444. године“. The interval is widened to hold both years and neither is chosen (5 October 2026).

hymns.text: Îndreptătorule al Ortodoxiei, învăţătorule al dreptei cinstiri de Dumnezeu şi al curaţiei şi luminătorule al lumii, podoaba călugărilor cea de Dumnezeu insuflată Sfinte Ierarhe Chiril, înţelepte, cu învăţăturile tale pe toţi i-ai luminat. Alăută duhovnicească, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Chiril, Arhiepiscopul Alexandriei, Glasul 8

english.text: O guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of the right worship of God and of purity, and light of the world, God-inspired adornment of monks, O wise hierarch Cyril: by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all. O spiritual harp, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Adâncul învăţăturilor cuvântării de Dumnezeu, lămurit ne-ai izvorât nouă din izvoarele Mântuitorului, care îneacă eresurile, fericite şi turma nevătămată de întreitele valuri o păzeşte; că marginilor eşti învăţător, ca cel ce arăţi cele dumnezeieşti.

source.text: Doxologia — Condacul Sfântului Ierarh Chiril, Arhiepiscopul Alexandriei, Glasul 6, «Plinind rânduiala cea pentru...»

english.text: Thou hast poured out for us clearly, from the Saviour's own springs, the depth of the teachings of theology, which drowns the heresies, O blessed one, and keeps the flock unharmed by the threefold waves; for thou art a teacher to the ends of the earth, as one who shows forth the things of God.

hymns.text: Ἒργοις λάμψαντες, Ὀρθοδοξίας, πᾶσαν σβέσαντες κακοδοξίαν, νικηταί τροπαιοφόροι γεγόνατε· τῇ εὐσεβείᾳ τά πάντα πλουτίσαντες, τήν Ἐκκλησίαν μεγάλως κοσμήσαντες, ἀξίως εὕρατε Χριστόν τόν Θεόν, δωρούμενον πᾶσι τό μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, «Θείας πίστεως», on the page of Άγιοι Αθανάσιος ο Μέγας και Κύριλλος Πατριάρχες Αλεξανδρείας; the hymn is the common of the two hierarchs kept on this day and is in the plural throughout

english.text: Shining forth in your works of Orthodoxy and quenching every false teaching, ye became victors and bearers of the trophy; having enriched all things with true worship and greatly adorned the Church, ye worthily found Christ God, who grants great mercy unto all.

hymns.text: Ἱεράρχαι μέγιστοι τῆς εὐσεβείας, καί γενναῖοι πρόμαχοι, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ, πάντας φρουρεῖτε τούς ψάλλοντας· Σῶσον οἰκτίρμον, τούς πίστει τιμῶντάς σε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, «Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον», on the page of Άγιοι Αθανάσιος ο Μέγας και Κύριλλος Πατριάρχες Αλεξανδρείας; the hymn is the common of the two hierarchs kept on this day

english.text: Greatest hierarchs of true worship and brave champions of the Church of Christ, guard all those who sing: Save, O compassionate one, those who honour thee in faith.

hymns.text: Православия наставниче,/ благочестия учителю и чистоты,/ вселенныя светильниче,/ архиереов богодухновенное удобрение,/ Кирилле премудре,/ ученьми твоими вся просветил еси,/ цевнице духовная,// моли Христа Бога спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителя Кирилла Александрийского», глас 8, printed in the day page’s «Молитвы» block. It names him, «Кирилле премудре».

english.text: Teacher of Orthodoxy, instructor in piety and purity, lamp of the whole world, God-inspired adornment of bishops, most wise Cyril: by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all things, O harp of the Spirit; entreat Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Бездну нам учений богословия источил еси/ яве от источник Спасовых,/ ереси погружающую,/ блаженне Кирилле,/ и стадо невредимо от треволнений спасающую,/ странам бо всем наставник, преподобне,// яко Божественная являя.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак святителя Кирилла Александрийского», глас 6, printed in the day page’s «Молитвы» block. It names him, «блаженне Кирилле».

english.text: Thou hast poured out for us an abyss of the teachings of theology, drawn plainly from the springs of the Saviour, which drowns the heresies and saves the flock unharmed from the surge of the waves; for thou art, O venerable one, the teacher of every land, showing forth the things of God, blessed Cyril.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 июня ст. ст. — «Свт. Кирилла , архиеп. Александрийского (444).»

attestations.note: The day's second entry. The Serbian row below already stands on this same Julian 9 June, from the Охридски пролог, and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on 18 January, which name page 1221 also lists: «Дни памяти: 18 января , 9 июня». Of those two the day read is 9 июня, and the 18 января Russian day page was not read; where the January day is the joint commemoration with Athanasius the Great that the Greek row quotes, this June day is his own. The year 444 agrees with this folder's `dates` and nothing in them was touched. Two hymns the day page sets over him by name are added with their English typed; the troparion is the common of a hierarch with his name filled into it, which BRIEF.md §4 makes his own service, and the kontakion is proper to him and names the heresies he sank. The life behind index id1221 was NOT read: the folder already carries a long life from the Great Synaxarion and from saint.gr, and this upgrade adds the Russian day, the Russian name form and the Russian hymns only. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 18 ianuarie — «Sfântul Ierarh Chiril, Arhiepiscopul Alexandriei»

attestations.note: Kept on 18 ianuarie with St Athanasius; the life on the same site says this is not the day of his repose and that he is also commemorated on 9 June, which it gives as the day he left this world. The hymn page marks the day ✝.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Ιανουαρίου — «Άγιοι Αθανάσιος ο Μέγας και Κύριλλος Πατριάρχες Αλεξανδρείας»

attestations.note: Commemorated with St Athanasius the Great. The same page (https://www.saint.gr/1127/saint.aspx) says that St Cyril is kept also on 9 June — «ο Άγιος Κύριλλος, εορτάζεται και στις 9 Ιουνίου» — and its epigram for today names this day as the memory of his flight and not of his repose: «Φυγῆς Κυρίλλου σήμερον μνήμην ἄγει, Ἀλλ' οὐ τελευτῆς τῆς ἀειμνήστου κτίσις.» It gives the repose as 27 June 444, where doxologia.ro, cited on this folder's Romanian row, gives 446 and 9 June; the readings are left standing side by side and the folder's dates are not changed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.06.2026 (9. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети Кирил, архиепископ александријски“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE DAY IS THE ONE THE ROMANIAN LIFE SAYS IT SHOULD BE, AND THE TWO OTHER ROWS ARE ON ANOTHER. doxologia and saint.gr both keep him on 18 JANUARY, and **this folder’s own `death` note already records that doxologia says otherwise about the day**: that the day of his repose is 9 June, on the authority of Christopher of Mitylene’s distich, and that 18 January is not the day of his repose. **This book keeps the Julian 9 June**, so the `serbian` row is on the day the Romanian page argued for while the Romanian row sits on the day the Romanian calendar prints. `sr-cand.mjs 01-18` prints this book’s own Julian 18 January, which is Athanasius the Great and Maximus archbishop of Vlach-Zaplanina, **and does not name him**, so there is no second Serbian day and no §4 note is owed. A DEATH WIDENED BY TWO YEARS. The folder held `death` 446, off the life’s note 71 quoting Theophanes the Confessor: «În acest an (446), au murit întru cucernicie Chiril al Alexandriei și Proclu al Constantinopolului». This book states „Представио се Господу 444. године“. Two books, two flat years: `death` 444 to 446, display «444 or 446», neither chosen. `birth` 378 untouched, this book giving no year of birth. ONE NEW `related` PAIR, RECIPROCAL, AND THE FOLDER IT REACHES HAD NONE. The entry says Cyril presided at the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus **and at the same time represented Celestine, pope of Rome, at that pope’s own request, he being too old to come to the Council**. `celestine-of-rome` exists, has `related: null`, and is reached by nothing. **A Council is not a folder and this row is not written on the Council**: it is written on a request one man made of another and a representation the body narrates. Added here and on his. A KINSHIP THE BODY NARRATES AND NO FOLDER TO PUT IT ON. „близак сродник Теофила, патријарха александријског, после чије смрти би посвећен за патријарха“ — a close kinsman of Theophilus, patriarch of Alexandria, whom he succeeded. **A kinship is the test that owes a row**, and `ls saints | grep -i '^theophilus'` returns twenty-odd folders of whom not one is the patriarch of Alexandria. Refused by ruling 3 and named. WHAT ELSE IS NEW, AND IT IS A GREAT DEAL. The three fights of his life set out as three: the Novatians, Nestorius, and the Jews of Alexandria. **The Novatian doctrine in detail** — named after the presbyter Novatian at Rome, proud of their own virtue, going about in white clothing, forbidding a second marriage, holding that one must not pray for those who commit a mortal sin nor take back into the church those who once fall away from it, however bitterly they repent — and that Cyril beat them and drove them out of Alexandria **together with their bishop**. **The fight with the Jews of Alexandria, which it calls much harder and bloodier**, and that he at last prevailed with the emperor Theodosius the Younger that they be driven out of the city. **That he presided at Ephesus and represented the pope.** **The end of Nestorius**: condemned, anathematised, exiled by the emperor to the eastern frontier of the empire, where he died a horrible death, worms eating the tongue with which he had blasphemed the Most Holy Theotokos by calling her Христородица, Christotokos. And, in the entry’s last sentence, **that he is said to have composed „Богородице Дјево радујся!“** — Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos. **THAT LAST IS A HYMN AND IT GOES NOWHERE NEAR `hymns`.** §3 of the Serbian brief is absolute: this source prints no liturgical text, and what it prints here is a claim about authorship and not the text of anything. `hymns` is untouched, nothing was quoted as a troparion, and the attribution is in the prose where a reader can weigh «it is said» for himself. `types` and `office` UNTOUCHED: архиепископ is the «Archbishop of Alexandria» `office` already holds, and `archbishop` is not added because the folder’s grade is `patriarch`, which is higher, and the 2 June refusal of a plain `martyr` beside a `great-martyr` is the same mechanism. NO ROWS for Nestorius, Novatian, the Novatian bishop or the Jews of Alexandria: no folder holds the first two, the third is unnamed, and the emperor Theodosius the Younger is already in this folder’s `related` off another page and takes no row for being an emperor here. No `locations`. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE AND FIVE WIDE, WHICH IS THE WIDEST THIS WAVE HAS WRITTEN. `foldchk.py` returns `cyril-of-catania`, `cyril-of-heliopolis`, `cyril-of-jerusalem` and `cyril-the-philosopher`, all four `sr`, for «Кирил». The see came off as §6 and five earlier days of this wave require, and the heading has nothing else in it, so there is nothing to break the fold with; the five are told apart by their sees and their days. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.
